correctness.rationale: The frozen claim fails as stated: the average of the two singlet tilings is a trace-one translation-invariant witness with a=0, b=−1, below the claimed minimum −1/(4π). The article's printed equation (11) was transcribed correctly but is inconsistent with equations (6) and (10) in standard Pauli normalization. The repaired result computes the actual minimum by the open-chain variational limit. The open-chain Jordan–Wigner hopping is 2, and the centered paired modes have minimum −4√(cos²q+γ²sin²q); closing the fermionic ring costs only O(1) in total energy. The limit is −4E/π, a factor of 16 correction. The normalized projected intercept is −4/π and the curvature coefficient is π/4 rather than 4π. The DLMF expansion gives ε''∼−(4/π)log(1/|γ|); the repaired verification also obtains this directly by comparison with t²/(t²+γ²)^{3/2}. The unique exposed point has a=ε'(γ), and the inverse support map gives g''=−1/ε'' away from zero. At zero g'' extends continuously with value zero but its difference quotient is unbounded. In the local algebraic obstruction, choosing the lowest weighted order i+2j and highest log power j gives a unique dominant monomial, so no nonzero polynomial can vanish on the one-sided graph.
residual_risks: The conclusion is for trace-one states and the displayed standard Pauli observables. Other scalings give other curvature coefficients. Verification of the repair is analytic; no formal-verification or expert certification is claimed.

value.rationale: The isotropic point is distinguished by the known anisotropy singularity, not picked arbitrarily. The law identifies how a diverging support susceptibility becomes vanishing curvature on a C² but not C³ reduced-state boundary, and fixes its coefficient in physically specified coordinates. It also gives a correct local proof of the claimed non-semialgebraicity while identifying both the normalization and analyticity defects of the motivating application. The gain is more than a scalar correction or replotting a known curve.
residual_risks: This is local geometry for a two-observable projection, not a general classification of reduced-state boundary singularities or an affine-invariant curvature statement.
